clue.text: What footballers may do with lifting gear

definitions.meaning: footballers stop an opponent's shot and challenge for the ball
a pulley system with rope used for hoisting loads

explanation.definitionFit: Footballers block shots and tackle opponents; the same phrase names a hoisting rig of pulleys and rope.

clue.text: Thief dressed in scarlet

indicators.note: dressed suggests these letters are arranged or prepared into a new order

explanation.surface: A robber is spotted wearing red clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' reads as wearing, but 'dressed' is the anagram signal working on the letters of IN SCARLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is the legal term for theft, so one who commits it is a stealer.

clue.text: Worries about God

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
Ares is the Greek god of war

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious about a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun synonym: anxieties or concerns.

clue.text: Colour found by painter that's used in perfumery

parts.note: amber is a yellowish-orange colour
Juan Gris was a Spanish Cubist painter

explanation.surface: A shade chosen by an artist turns out to be a scent ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' and 'that's' are link words joining the charade to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxy substance from sperm whales, valued as a fixative in scent-making.

clue.text: A mournful piece of music, dreadful around midnight

indicators.note: around tells us one word wraps about the other

parts.note: dreadful means dire
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A sad tune is terrible when played late at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' means the middle of the word night, its letter G, which goes inside DIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament sung or played at a funeral.

clue.text: Doubtful gain by king's men in battle?

indicators.note: doubtful hints that the letters of gain are uncertain in their order

parts.note: a king's attendants form his court

explanation.surface: A dubious profit for royal retainers in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtful' looks like a comment on the gain but is the anagram signal. The question mark warns that the battle is a famous 1415 English victory in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the 1415 battle won by Henry V's army.

clue.text: Poet takes liberty

indicators.note: taking a liberty with letters means treating them freely, so their order changes

explanation.surface: A versifier is being presumptuous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes liberty' reads as a phrase meaning presumes, but 'liberty' signals an anagram of TAKES.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: John Keats, English Romantic writer of odes.

clue.text: Measure 19 down — it needs to be revised

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of width
the answer to 19 down, in its sense of halted, means finished

explanation.surface: A gauge for a neighbouring clue needs editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it needs to be' is link material; the definition is just 'revised'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: corrected or edited text.

clue.text: Minister soft on crime

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes before

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: A clergyman is lenient towards wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a parish clergyman ministers to his flock.

clue.text: River runs dry using this

parts.note: the Aire is a river in Yorkshire
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A watercourse runs out of water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as an instruction: what you dry clothes with.
explanation.definitionFit: A rack or frame on which laundry is hung to dry.

clue.text: Stinker constrained by writer's block

indicators.note: constrained by means held within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish author of Peter Pan
a cad is a rotter or stinker

explanation.surface: A rogue is held back by an author unable to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer's block' looks like one phrase, but 'block' is the definition and 'writer's' gives BARRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an obstruction set up to stop passage.

clue.text: Poet with swollen head writes to the queen

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to pen is to write
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A bigheaded bard sends letters to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swollen head' suggests vanity, but means the first letter of swollen. ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Edmund Spenser, Elizabethan author of The Faerie Queene.

clue.text: Tax on diamonds must be removed

parts.note: excise is a duty on goods
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A levy on gems must be abolished.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: cut out, as of a passage or tissue.

clue.text: We hear no beastly noise

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: Someone denies hearing an animal's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry a horse makes, an animal sound.

clue.text: Uriah's oil rig? Very funny!

indicators.note: to rig is to fix or arrange, so the letters before are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its s, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone owns a drilling platform, and it's a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil rig' reads as one thing, but 'rig' is the anagram signal on URIAHS OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: extremely amusing, side-splitting.

clue.text: What reporter did with crude note to be edited

indicators.note: editing changes text around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A journalist's rough memo is to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be edited' rearranges CRUDE NOTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter related or narrated events, past tense.

clue.text: Cocky prisoner in the chair, we hear

parts.note: con is short for convict

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: being in a chair means sitting down

explanation.surface: A brash convict is sitting presiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the chair' suggests presiding, but means sitting; that word said out loud is spelt CEITED here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: arrogant, full of oneself.

clue.text: Bird goes to Newcastle area

parts.note: to have a go is to take a turn, so goes are turns
taken as written
Newcastle is in the north-east of England

explanation.surface: A bird flies off to Tyneside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading shorebird that flips stones to find food.

clue.text: The bench takes offence but adapts to new environment

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden seat
a sin is a wrong or offence

explanation.surface: A judge's court objects but adjusts to change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The bench' suggests judges in court; here it is a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb synonym: becomes accustomed or at home.

clue.text: Spinner raced round, being wound up

indicators.note: round means one word goes about the other

parts.note: sped means raced
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A spinning toy rushed about until its spring was wound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' reads as tightened, but means ended.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concluded or brought to an end, as in a meeting halted.

clue.text: Brief encountered in quarter sessions

indicators.note: encountered in means the word is met within the clue's letters

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns up at a local court sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' suggests a barrister; it is an adjective. Quarter sessions were old English courts held four times a year.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: concise, short and to the point.

clue.text: Most of Stevenson's characters are all the same

indicators.note: most of means only part of the name's letters are taken
characters means letters of the name, not people in books

explanation.surface: Many of a novelist's creations are alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' suggests people in Robert Louis Stevenson's novels, but means his name's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: nevertheless, despite that.

clue.text: Volunteered to get away before grand finale

parts.note: off means away
ere is poetic for before

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone stepped forward to escape before the big ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: proposed or tendered willingly.

clue.text: Currency a country finally abandoned

indicators.note: finally abandoned means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A money unit that one nation eventually gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: France gave up its money for the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the former French unit of money.

clue.text: Spirit revealed by music presenter in Beethoven's ninth

parts.note: a DJ is a disc jockey
taken as written

indicators.note: the ninth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A ghost appears via a DJ playing Beethoven's Ninth Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's ninth' suggests the symphony, but means letter nine of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie of Arabian folklore, a supernatural being.

clue.text: Man sees constituents all together

indicators.note: constituents are component parts, so the letters are taken and recombined

explanation.surface: An MP meets the voters in a body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests voters, but signals the letters of MAN SEES rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as a group, all at once.

clue.text: Instant tea or coffee

parts.note: mo is short for moment
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Choosing between powdered drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' suggests powdered coffee, but means a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a type of coffee, often with chocolate.

clue.text: Philosopher resolving last point

indicators.note: resolving means breaking down and reforming, so letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A thinker settles the final issue.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Plato's teachings.

clue.text: To make these, cobbler must start with bits of wood

definitions.text: To make these, cobbler must start with bits of wood

indicators.note: must start means only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: logs are pieces of wood

explanation.surface: A shoemaker begins making wooden footwear from timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes wooden shoes while also building them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden-soled shoes, made by a cobbler from timber.

clue.text: Avoid beach? Navigator's game

parts.note: to duck is to dodge
sand covers a beach
Sir Francis Drake was an Elizabethan navigator

explanation.surface: Dodge the shore? A seafarer's pastime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastime of skimming flat stones over water.
